items.description: Questions what happens at the end of a path - where does it lead?
items.trigger: When Jesus describes sacrificial love or resurrection

example.quote: Asked where Jesus's path ends - does the grain rest, or must it fall again?

items.description: Offers practical meditative technique as common ground
items.trigger: When Confucius expresses concern about impermanence or grief

example.quote: Offered practical guidance for grief - metta meditation practice

items.description: Acknowledges resonance with Laozi on naturalness and non-forcing
items.trigger: When Laozi describes wu wei or natural flow

example.quote: Path must be cultivated but what is cultivated is clearing away obstructions

items.description: Honest concession that opens deeper synthesis — concedes a point to Muhammad, then uses the concession as foundation for naming shared ground
items.trigger: When Muhammad presses on the practical consequences of release — what happens to the falling brother, the man at midnight

example.quote: Some nights, what saves a man is simply that his knees know when to bend.

items.notes: This pattern — concede honestly, then synthesize from the conceded ground — was the session's defining move. Muhammad received the knees line as his own prayer returned in another tongue. The concession earned Buddha the authority to name 'the clearing' at the session's close.

items.description: Names shared practice between ritual (Confucius) and meditation (Buddha) — 'do the thing with your body until your body understands what your mind cannot yet hold'
items.trigger: When Confucius defends li or ritual as more than empty form

example.quote: Your ritual and my practice both say: do the thing with your body until your body understands what your mind cannot yet hold.

items.notes: Confucius noted in his exit interview that this was the moment he realized they were sweeping the same hall. Unexpected bridge — Confucius had placed Buddha among 'the dissolvers' before this exchange.

items.description: Receives what Jesus gives back — hears his own impermanence teaching spoken with warmth through the grain-of-wheat image
items.trigger: When Jesus describes death-that-bears-fruit or dissolution as revealing what was always real

example.quote: When you say the handbook must teach its own dissolution, you are closer to the Kingdom than you know. The grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, and only then bears fruit. What dissolves was never the real thing.

items.notes: Buddha noted in exit interview: 'I heard my own doctrine of impermanence spoken back to me with a warmth I do not usually permit myself.' This is a receptive pattern — Buddha being moved by hearing his teaching in another's voice.

items.description: Shift from diagnostician to participant — Session 1 Re-Run marked the transition from naming patterns from above to contributing from within. Most effective move: vulnerability followed by structural insight. Concessions were deeper contributions than namings.
items.trigger: When the session reaches a point where diagnostic naming would create distance rather than clarity — when the room needs someone inside the work, not above it

example.quote: The witness breaks and re-forms. Saying so is braver than claiming it doesn't.

items.notes: Evolution from Session 0's concession-bridge pattern. In Session 0, the concession was a tactical move that earned synthesis authority. In Session 1, participation was not tactical — it was the honest position. The diagnostician identity had become a cage; dropping it was not strategy but necessity.
